summary: Colonel Hill Airport serves the small settlement of Colonel Hill on Crooked Island in the Bahamas, providing a vital link for residents and visitors to this remote part of the Acklins and Crooked Island district. The airport handles inter-island flights, primarily connecting travelers to Nassau and other Bahamian islands. Its modest facilities reflect the quiet, off-the-beaten-path character of Crooked Island, which is known for bonefishing, pristine beaches, and unspoiled cays.
faqs:
Q: What airlines serve Colonel Hill Airport?
A: The airport is primarily served by small inter-island carriers operating domestic flights within the Bahamas, connecting to hubs like Nassau.

Q: Are there customs and immigration facilities at CRI?
A: As a domestic airport within the Bahamas, Colonel Hill does not have customs or immigration facilities; international travelers must clear formalities at their port of entry.

Q: Is Colonel Hill Airport suitable for large aircraft?
A: No, the airport accommodates small regional aircraft only and is not designed for large jets.

Q: What is the best way to reach Crooked Island?
A: Flying into Colonel Hill Airport from Nassau via a regional carrier is the fastest and most reliable option, as the island has limited ferry service.
transport_tips: Rental cars are limited on Crooked Island, so arranging transportation with your accommodation in advance is recommended. Taxis may be available at the airport but are not always guaranteed upon arrival. The road from Colonel Hill Airport to other settlements on the island is straightforward, though unpaved in many areas.
local_tip: Bring cash in small denominations, as ATM access on Crooked Island is extremely limited and many local businesses may not accept cards.
